arxiv-2209-03019.title: Fundamentals of Stellar Parameters Estimation through CMD of Star Clusters: Open (NGC 2360) and Globular (NGC 5272)
arxiv-2209-03019.creator: Kanwar Preet Kaur, Pankaj S. Joshi
arxiv-2209-03019.description: Abstract The fundamentals of estimating essential stellar parameters of an open cluster - NGC 2360 and globular clusters - NGC 5272 are presented extensively in this work. Here, the evaluation of stellar parameters, by manually fitting the appropriate isochrones on the color magnitude diagrams (CMDs), of the selected star clusters is discussed comprehensively.

arxiv-2212-08032.title: Demonstration of machine-learning-enhanced Bayesian quantum state estimation
arxiv-2212-08032.creator: Sanjaya Lohani, Joseph M. Lukens, Atiyya A. Davis, Amirali Khannejad, Sangita Regmi, Daniel E. Jones, Ryan T. Glasser, Thomas A. Searles, Brian T. Kirby
arxiv-2212-08032.description: Abstract Machine learning (ML) has found broad applicability in quantum information science in topics as diverse as experimental design, state classification, and even studies on quantum foundations. Here, we experimentally realize an approach for defining custom prior distributions that are automatically tuned using ML for use with Bayesian quantum state estimation methods.

arxiv-2310-19994.title: Proton and carbon-ion minibeam therapy: from modeling to treatment E-mail: pshenich@inr.ru
arxiv-2310-19994.description: Abstract Arrays of minibeams of protons and 12 C in tissue-like media were modeled with Geant4 toolkit. A set of beam energies was used in simulations to provide a Spead-out Bragg peak (SOBP) extended by 6 cm in depth for protons as well as for 12 C. In both cases, beams of 0.3 mm or 0.

arxiv-2405-18549.title: Learning from Uncertain Data: From Possible Worlds to Possible Models
arxiv-2405-18549.creator: Jiongli Zhu, Su Feng, Boris Glavic, Babak Salimi
arxiv-2405-18549.description: Abstract We introduce an efficient method for learning linear models from uncertain data, where uncertainty is represented as a set of possible variations in the data, leading to predictive multiplicity. Our approach leverages abstract interpretation and zonotopes, a type of convex polytope, to compactly represent these dataset variations, enabling the symbolic execution of gradient descent on all possible worlds simultaneously.

arxiv-2502-14051.title: RocketKV: Accelerating Long-Context LLM Inference via Two-Stage KV Cache Compression
arxiv-2502-14051.creator: Payman Behnam, Yaosheng Fu, Ritchie Zhao, Po-An Tsai, Zhiding Yu, Alexey Tumanov
arxiv-2502-14051.description: Abstract Transformer-based Large Language Models rely critically on the KV cache to efficiently handle extended contexts during the decode phase. Yet, the size of the KV cache grows proportionally with the input length, burdening both memory bandwidth and capacity as decoding progresses. To address this challenge, we present RocketKV, a training-free KV cache compression strategy containing two consecutive stages.

arxiv-2503-04705.title: One Extension to Explain Them All, One Scale-Invariant Spectrum to Test Them All, and in One Model Bind Them
arxiv-2503-04705.creator: Matteo Forconi, Eleonora Di Valentino
arxiv-2503-04705.description: Abstract The increasing precision of Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) observations has unveiled significant tensions between different datasets, notably between Planck and the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT), as well as with late-Universe measurements of the Hubble constant. In this work, we explore a variety of beyond- Λ \Lambda CDM extensions to assess their ability to reconcile these discrepancies.

arxiv-2506-10305.title: Self-learning signal classifier for decameter coherent scatter radars
arxiv-2506-10305.creator: Oleg Berngardt, Ivan Lavygin, et al
arxiv-2506-10305.description: Abstract The paper presents a method for automatic constructing a classifier for processed data obtained by decameter coherent scatter radars. Method is based only on the radar data obtained, the results of automatic modeling of radio wave propagation in the ionosphere, and mathematical criteria for estimating the quality of the models.

arxiv-2511-16206.title: A pilot very long baseline interferometry study of the SQUAB quasar sample featuring multiple Gaia detections
arxiv-2511-16206.creator: Y. Zhang, T. An, X. Ji, Z. Zheng, Y. Liu, Q. Wu, R. Lin, S. Liao
arxiv-2511-16206.description: Abstract Context. Our previous work identified a class of SDSS quasars with multiple Gaia detections, classifying them as candidates for various astrophysical systems, such as quasar–star pairs, dual quasars, and gravitationally lensed quasars. In this paper we present a pilot very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) study targeting a radio-bright subsample and report the first high-resolution imaging results. Aims.

arxiv-2512-21416.title: Observation of disorder-induced superfluidity
arxiv-2512-21416.creator: Google Quantum AI and collaborators †
arxiv-2512-21416.description: Abstract The emergence of states with long-range correlations in a disordered landscape is rare, as disorder typically suppresses the particle mobility required for long-range coherence. But when more than two energy levels are available per site, disorder can induce resonances that locally enhance mobility.

pmc-11579604.title: Unhealthy food outlets and outdoor advertisements in urban South African primary school students’ food environments
pmc-11579604.creator: Michelle R Brear, Agnes Erzse, Glynis Clacherty, Lebogang Seutlwadi, Sameera Mahomedy, Kabelo Maleke, Susan Goldstein
pmc-11579604.description: Children’s exposure to outlets selling, and outdoor advertisements marketing, unhealthy foods is an important risk factor for obesity. Yet few policies address the food retail and/or outdoor advertising environment, and research about children’s perceptions is limited, especially in low- and middle-income countries.

pmc-11623314.title: Efficacy of Myofascial Release Therapy and Positional Release Therapy in Patients with Upper Trapezius Trigger Points: Study Protocol of a Double-blinded Randomized Clinical Trial
pmc-11623314.creator: Rubi Yadav, Sunita Sharma
pmc-11623314.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundMyofascial trigger points are incredibly prevalent and are a painful aspect of almost everyone’s life at some point. Myofascial trigger point pain can be excruciating and severely impair the quality of life. Therefore, in patients with neck pain caused by upper trapezius trigger, this current clinical trial will demonstrate the effectiveness of myofascial release therapy and positional release therapy in improving the level of pain, neck impairment, pain threshold, and standard of life.MethodsA double-blinded randomized clinical trial will be conducted.

pmc-12524366.title: Psychological, Symptom-Related, and Lifestyle Predictors of Health-Related Quality of Life in Hungarian Women with Endometriosis
pmc-12524366.creator: Zsófia Kovács-Szabó, Pongrác Ács, Viktória Prémusz, Alexandra Makai, Márta Hock, Simone Ferrero
pmc-12524366.description: Background: This study was a cross-sectional online survey aimed at examining health-related quality of life and the effect of different symptoms and lifestyle factors on health-related quality of life in a sample of women with endometriosis in Hungary. Methodology: A cross-sectional online survey was carried out in a sample of women with endometriosis.

pmc-13208719.title: A Technical Feasibility Study of the Recovery of Used Lubricant Oil Using Ceramic Ultrafiltration Membranes
pmc-13208719.creator: Madina Mohamed, Pieter Vandezande, Anita Buekenhoudt
pmc-13208719.description: This laboratory-scale experimental study investigated the purification level of used lubricant oil (ULO) filtration using a large variety of ceramic UF membranes, allowing for treatment at high temperatures unreachable for polymeric membranes. Varying pore sizes (5 nm, 10 nm, 30 nm, and 100 nm) were included as well as a range of materials (Al2O3, TiO2, and ZrO2).

pmc-13258677.title: Evaluating the Ability of Multimodal Artificial Intelligence to Identify Endodontic Instruments: A Comparative Study of ChatGPT-4o and Gemini 3 Flash
pmc-13258677.creator: Samet Tosun, Emre Çulha
pmc-13258677.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background/Objectives: Multimodal large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into dental diagnostics. This study evaluated the ability of ChatGPT-4o and Gemini 3 Flash to visually identify endodontic instruments and assess their explanatory plausibility regarding instrument morphology. Methods: Standardized images of five endodontic file systems (Reciproc R25, Reciproc Blue, WaveOne Gold, MM One Shape, and XP-endo Finisher) were submitted to both models via their free tiers.

pmc-13453087.title: Fisetin alleviates zinc overload-induced intestinal injury by inhibiting ferroptosis and remodeling gut microbiota in weaned piglets
pmc-13453087.creator: Feifei Huang, Yuhang Deng, Mohan Zhou, Huangen Xu, Jie Feng
pmc-13453087.description: BackgroundHigh doses of zinc oxide (ZnO) effectively prevent post-weaning diarrhea and promote growth in weaned piglets, but raise concerns over intestinal injury, metabolic disorders, and risks of fostering bacterial resistance. This study aimed to identify non-chelating polyphenols capable of mitigating zinc toxicity and to elucidate their protective mechanisms, with emphasis on ferroptosis inhibition.

pmc-13540589.title: Comparative Analysis of Clinicopathological Features and Outcomes Between Kidney-Limited and Systemic Thrombotic Microangiopathy: A Study Based on a Semiquantitative Pathological Scoring System
pmc-13540589.creator: Yan Pan, Yongxin Zhao, Xi Li, Xueping Wu, Bowen Chen, Mengru Lu, Rubing Shen, WeiDong Chen, Lei Liu
pmc-13540589.description: ObjectiveTo systematically compare the clinicopathological features and prognostic outcomes of renal-limited thrombotic microangiopathy (RL-TMA) and systemic thrombotic microangiopathy (Sys-TMA) using a semiquantitative pathological scoring system.MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed 47 patients with biopsy-proven TMA between 2018 and 2025, categorized as RL-TMA (n = 42) or Sys-TMA (n = 5) based on systemic manifestations. Clinical, pathological, and follow-up data were collected.
